title: Preserve existing Snapper retention policy
head: 500fd6a05f0b
workflow: Early pipeline: one or two Claude technical reviewers, coordinator synthesis, editorial check

prior_findings.claim: Failed first initialization is not repaired by retry; an intermediate config is preserved instead of applying Omarchy defaults.
prior_findings.reason: Marked initialization retains ownership after failed template installation; retry installs exact Omarchy defaults and clears marker without another create-config call. Original behavior independently reproduced.

limits: Synthetic Snapper creation and recorded systemctl, no real Btrfs or service mutation.
No full shell suite or complete installer/upgrade.
Old unmarked intermediate configs remain preserved.
Astra supplied-suite run dependency-limited; Fable related suites used pinned companion inputs.
retro:
# Retrospective

- Matching the public failure condition on original and current pinned snapshots yielded a clear resolution without live Snapper or desktop resources.
- Independent fixtures agreed. Testing the actual logging helper and testing regression sensitivity beyond marker existence added useful confidence.
- Equivalent neutral assignments and fresh native sessions preserved independence. Both complete reports were read before synthesis.
- Avoidable setup friction: a whole-source archive rejected an absolute plugin symlink. The failed run was preserved; a scoped clean source archive succeeded. This is a documented boundary, not a confirmed tool bug.
- Companion inputs were absent from the neutral packet. Astra correctly recorded dependency-limited supplied-suite execution; Fable fetched/pinned sufficient packaging/ISO inputs and completed related suites. Future packets can include neutral dependency pins, without requiring unrelated suite execution.
- Carry forward the distinction between initialization begun on the corrected revision and historical unmarked intermediate configs. The latter cannot be safely inferred from policy values.
- No Omadev issue observed, no desktop slot used. No safety deviation or host mutation reported. All runtime tests went through review.py; failed setup and raw failed producer evidence remain intact.
- Technical artifacts, source snapshots, session records and exact editorial inputs are retained. HTML was not opened. No upstream action was taken.
comment:
**Verified:** the [previous recovery finding](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12598#issuecomment-5759290763) is resolved at `500fd6a0` for initialization started with this revision. No new actionable issue was found in the directly affected scope.

With a recording Snapper substitute creating the intermediate policy and real GNU `install` failing on a missing template:

```text
Retry after restoring the template    Previous 784664c2     Current 500fd6a0
Final NUMBER_LIMIT                    50 (intermediate)    5 (exact Omarchy template)
Additional create-config calls        0                    0
Initialization marker                 not tracked          removed after success
```

The marker survives the first failed installation. Existing unmarked policies still retain their bytes and permissions across repeated configuration. The new recovery regression rejects the previous implementation and passes on the current head.

This does not retroactively identify unfinished configs left by older revisions without a marker; those remain preserved as unmarked policies.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** real configuration script, Bash and GNU `install`, with synthetic Snapper creation and recorded service commands. No real Btrfs operations, snapshot deletion, service changes, full shell suite or complete upgrade tested.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra coordination and source inspection, fresh independent Fable 5.1 High and Astra Xhigh follow-up reviews with separate experiments, followed by evidence reconciliation and a fresh Astra Medium editorial check.
